answer: The most convincing defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals its account age times verified honest epochs, so a fresh sybil identity starts near zero and cannot buy or fake seniority. Like an island emerging from a lagoon, reputation rises only through long, verifiable participation, one honest ledge at a time. An attacker must keep many accounts alive and honest for months at real operational cost, and any detected fraud slashes the whole lineage, making mass fake identities economically pointless.
